The narrower and supportable position is that the packet can defend a caveated certification record only if it expressly states three things already supported by the admissible evidence: aggregate readiness passed, the exposed legal-intake-triage segment remains below target and is still in scope for the initial rollout, and the policy therefore requires explicit model-card disclosure because there is no approved risk acceptance covering that exposure. On that framing, the packet is not claiming the controls satisfy the policy exception; it is claiming the limitation is being disclosed while deployment risk is managed through staged rollout and monitoring.

The defensible packet therefore must not argue that controls alone make the release compliant; it should argue only that any certification record must be caveated by explicit model-card disclosure of the unresolved legal-intake-triage limitation and by accurate description of the exposed rollout condition.
